hypotheses.claim: slice tab=0 scores 0.3044 vs overall 0.6191 across 5579 users; a feature or prior targeted at this slice should close part of the gap

evidence.finding: 56% of the gain survives surface scrambling: mechanism revised from surface familiarity to partitioned familiarity (about half surface-specific, half counting structure). Promotion unaffected (validation-based).

control.detail: R33-placebo valid 0.61612 vs control 0.61715: the entire +0.0024 gain collapses when the per-surface count is detached from its impression

hypotheses.claim: slice tab=1 scores 0.5949 vs overall 0.6191 across 20119 users; a feature or prior targeted at this slice should close part of the gap; oracle headroom on the overall metric 0.2128 (31% of the slice's users are all-negative inside it, so the slice-restricted score understates the model)

evidence.note: Claimable negative: -0.00347 clears the 0.002 gate, consistent across 3 seeds and both metric components (valid GAUC 0.68969 vs 0.69341, nDCG@5 0.54444 vs 0.54568). Session-local outcome momentum is a coarser, reset-on-gap duplicate of hist10/hist30.

evidence.finding: The within-visit fatigue effect is real and large marginally (tab=1 long_view rate 0.418 at session position 0 -> 0.143 at 50+, train rows) and 77% of its prior variance is WITHIN user, the only channel the metric scores; 54% of that within-user prior is not explained by the champion's features (R^2 0.46). For tab_n -- the feature that DID win, +0.0024 -- the same measurement gives 86% novel and 1.04e-04 of within-user prior variance, versus sess_pos's 8.19e-05: the same order. So a 'large, novel, within-user prior' screen would have rated sess_pos as promising as tab_n and been wrong. That screen is hereby falsified as a pre-run filter for this project.
evidence.scope: What is refuted is this INTERVENTION, not the slice's headroom: tab=1 is 73% of impressions and its oracle headroom (0.2113) is an arithmetic fact about slice size, not a defect the loop has explained away.
